newsitem.title: USA: CME traders call USDA hog data bullish for futures.
newsitem.headline: CME traders call USDA hog data bullish for futures.

text.p: CME livestock traders said the USDA Hogs and Pigs Report showed U.S. producers had not begun aggressively expanding hog herds as analysts had expected, which should be bullish for hog prices from now through early 1998.
The report showed hogs kept for breeding as June 1 increased one percent from a year ago versus analysts' forecasts for a three- to six-percent increase.
Traders expect CME July to October hog futures to trade 0.50 to 1.00 cent per lb higher early Monday and December and forward futures to rise the 2.00-cent daily limit.

In other key catagories the report showed the June 1 U.S. hog herd at 58.15 million head, up two percent from a year ago but slightly less than the 2.9-percent increase produced by averaging analysts' estimates. Hogs kept for market numbered 51.2 million head, up two percent from a year ago and slightly less than the analysts' average estimate for a 2.6-percent increase.
